paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to hold onto. Solomon built the temple, and he prayed, but he didn't make the fire. He finished praying, and then fire came down from heaven and the glory of the LORD filled the house (2 Chronicles 7:1). We do the work, and GOD is the one who shows up.

Look at what the people do when He does. They bow down with their faces to the ground and say, "For He is good; His loving devotion endures forever." (2 Chronicles 7:3). They don't start with a speech. They start with thanks, because He is good and His loving devotion doesn't run out. Then the whole thing keeps going, with offerings, trumpets and a feast of seven days (2 Chronicles 7:4-8), because when God is that good, a quick thank you just won't do it.

And see how they go home, friend: "joyful and glad of heart for the good things that the LORD had done" (2 Chronicles 7:10). Their joy comes from what He did, not from what they did. That's the kind of joy I want you walking out of the bakery with, a heart full of thanks for the One who is good. And hold onto it, because this story isn't over yet.
